metadata.title: EASL-ILCA Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
metadata.source: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) and International Liver Cancer Association (ILCA)
metadata.methodology: PICO framework, Oxford Centre for Evidence-based Medicine levels of evidence, Delphi consensus

who-classification.description: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is classified separately from perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinoma in ICD-11 and ICD-O-4

type.name: Periductal-infiltrating (PI)
type.description: Growth along bile duct wall causing stricture

type.name: Intraductal growing (IG)
type.description: Papillary growth within bile duct lumen

histological-subtypes.recommendation: Subclassification into large duct type and small duct type is suggested, as this may have clinical utility based on prognostic and therapeutic implications

features.feature: Arises from large intrahepatic bile ducts

subtype.name: Small duct type

features.feature: Arises from small intrahepatic bile ducts or hepatic progenitor cells

subtype.association: May arise in cirrhotic liver, often associated with chronic liver disease

histological-subtypes.recommendation: Macro classification is suggested in combination with pathological subclassification, as it is more reliable and reproducible

factor.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)
factor.notes: Leading risk factor in Western countries

factor.name: NAFLD/NASH
factor.notes: Emerging risk factor in Western countries

risk-factors.note: Risk factors identified in only ~30% of patients; most cases are sporadic

psc-patients.recommendation: Annual surveillance with non-invasive radiologic tools is suggested for patients with PSC
For surveillance of CCA in patients with PSC, MRI+MRCP is suggested as it has the highest diagnostic accuracy
psc-patients.tumor-markers: CA 19-9 as adjunct (limited sensitivity in early disease)

cirrhosis-patients.recommendation: Ultrasound at 6-monthly intervals is suggested for patients with cirrhosis, as it may be effective for detection of iCCA at an early stage
cirrhosis-patients.note: iCCA surveillance can be incorporated into HCC surveillance program

liver-fluke-endemic.recommendation: In patients infected with liver flukes, abdominal ultrasound surveillance at 6-monthly intervals is recommended
liver-fluke-endemic.program: Cholangiocarcinoma Screening and Care Program in Thailand

liver-fluke-prevention.recommendation: Educational campaigns may be considered as useful tools in changing behaviour to prevent liver fluke infection and re-infection
liver-fluke-prevention.program: Integrated health education approach in Thailand

strategies.strategy: Avoid consumption of raw or undercooked freshwater fish
Treatment of infected individuals with praziquantel

hepatolithiasis-management.recommendation: Given conflicting results and low quality of published studies, it is not possible to give a recommendation on hepatic resection as a strategy to prevent iCCA in patients with hepatolithiasis

biopsy.recommendation: Tumour biopsy is recommended to obtain a definitive diagnosis. Despite the low quality of evidence, this recommendation was proposed as strong as a definitive diagnosis has critical clinical relevance
biopsy.rationale: Required for histological confirmation and molecular profiling

immunohistochemistry.recommendation: Immunohistochemistry can be useful to confirm/diagnose iCCA and its subtypes in order to distinguish it from metastatic liver tumours

molecular-profiling.recommendation: In patients who are at high risk for recurrence (node or margin positive, vascular invasion, or multifocal intrahepatic disease), molecular profiling with a comprehensive panel is suggested at the time of diagnosis
NGS-based comprehensive genomic profiling recommended for advanced disease

imaging-for-staging.recommendation: MRI should be considered instead of CT scanning for staging iCCA within the liver

Given the strong role of PET scanning in identifying lymph node metastasis, patients with apparent resectable iCCA should routinely undergo FDG-PET scanning to identify lymph node metastases not apparent on standard CT or MRI during staging evaluation

Patients with apparent resectable iCCA should undergo lymph node sampling by EUS with fine needle aspiration to identify lymph node metastases during staging evaluation, if a positive result would alter management

t-stage.T1a: Solitary tumour ≤5 cm without vascular invasion
t-stage.T1b: Solitary tumour >5 cm without vascular invasion
t-stage.T2: Solitary tumour with intrahepatic vascular invasion or multiple tumours with or without vascular invasion
t-stage.T4: Tumour involving local extrahepatic structures by direct invasion

unresectable-disease.second-line: FOLFOX or targeted therapy based on molecular profile

resection.recommendation: Resection of iCCA may be considered in selected patients with multifocal, unilobar CCA

There is insufficient evidence supporting a recommendation for consideration of resection rather than locoregional and/or systemic treatments in patients with iCCA and macroscopic vascular involvement of the IVC, hepatic vein or portal vein

procedures.procedure: Anatomic hepatectomy preferred over non-anatomic resection
procedures.margin: R0 with ≥1 cm margin if achievable

alpps.recommendation: Not recommended for iCCA due to high morbidity/mortality

minimally-invasive.consideration: May be considered in experienced centres for selected patients

neoadjuvant-therapy.recommendation: Neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy can be considered in patients with technically challenging but resectable disease, if an R1 resection is likely to be achievable

adjuvant-therapy.recommendation: A 6-month course of oral fluoropyrimidine (capecitabine or S1) should be considered following potentially curative resection of iCCA

trial.name: BILCAP
trial.intervention: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1-14, q3w × 8 cycles
trial.result: Improved median OS (51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81)

early-icca-in-cirrhosis.recommendation: Liver transplantation for early stage iCCA (≤3 cm) arising in the setting of cirrhosis can be considered, preferably under study protocols

locally-advanced.recommendation: Liver transplantation for locally advanced iCCA should not be performed outside of clinical trials

unresectable-first-line.recommendation: Patients with unresectable iCCA and good performance status should be treated with GemCis (as first-line chemotherapy), with the addition of durvalumab where available

regimen.cycle: Every 3 weeks for 8 cycles, then durvalumab maintenance

unresectable-first-line.recommendation: In patients with iCCA and impaired performance status, gemcitabine monotherapy or plus S-1 combination therapy may provide comparable efficacy with fewer adverse events

second-line.recommendation: Patients with iCCA with good performance status who progressed on first-line therapy should be treated with: FOLFOX chemotherapy or ivosidenib for those with IDH1 mutations, FGFR inhibitors for those with FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements, and immune checkpoint blockade for those with dMMR/MSI-H who have not received durvalumab in first-line

fgfr-inhibitors.indication: FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements (10-15% of iCCA)
fgfr-inhibitors.recommendation: FGFR inhibitors should be recommended for patients with iCCA and FGFR2 fusions or other rearrangements after progression on standard first-line chemotherapy

drug.name: Ivosidenib
drug.evidence: Improved PFS vs placebo (2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37)

immunotherapy.recommendation: Immune checkpoint blockade in patients with iCCA and dMMR/MSI-H who have progressed on first-line chemotherapy should be considered a therapeutic option

transarterial-procedures.recommendation: Transarterial procedures (SIRT, chemoembolisation and intra-arterial chemotherapy) are feasible and safe, and may be a reasonable alternative in selected patients with unresectable disease

ablation.recommendation: In unresectable or inoperable patients with a single <2 cm iCCA, thermal ablation can be considered as a good alternative, as it is feasible and safe

radiotherapy.recommendation: Due to insufficient evidence, we cannot recommend in favour or against external beam ablative dose radiation therapy as an alternative to systemic therapy in unresectable liver-limited iCCA

recurrence-assessment.recommendation: The choice of the right liver imaging method to assess recurrence after surgery or interventional procedures with curative intent should consider technical issues related to different treatments. However, any imaging evaluation of the liver should always be complemented by a CT scan of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis since recurrence may occur inside or outside the liver

imaging-options.option: MRI for liver assessment (especially post-TACE, SIRT)
PET-CT may be useful for detecting recurrence

priority.name: Prevention
priority.description: Improved prevention strategies in liver fluke endemic areas
Addressing metabolic syndrome as emerging risk factor

priority.name: Early detection
priority.description: Development of circulating biomarkers (ctDNA, miRNA, proteins)
Improved surveillance protocols for high-risk populations

priority.name: Molecular medicine
priority.description: Up to 40% of iCCAs have targetable molecular alterations
New pathways being investigated for combination therapies
Precision medicine approach based on genomic, histologic, and clinical data

priority.name: Collaborative research
priority.description: International multicentre projects to overcome small case numbers
Translation from animal models to clinical practice
